```{r}
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Visit code", y = "Participants"
  ) 

```

### Harmonization of weekly and daily responses

In this section, we merge the information for `n_put_in_vagina` from the daily CRF33 and the weekly CRF21 into one single variable `n_put_in_vagina`.

```{r}

vaginal_insertions <- 
  vaginal_insertions |>
  mutate(
    n_put_in_vagina = coalesce(n_put_in_vagina.crf33, n_put_in_vagina.crf21)
  )

```


```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 8

vaginal_insertions |> 
  filter(!is.na(n_put_in_vagina)) |>
  filter(randomized) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(
    x = visit_code |> factor(), y = pid, 
    col = n_put_in_vagina |> factor()
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(site ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    "Number of vaginal insertions",
    values =
      c("0" = "transparent", "1" = "black", "2" = "#E69F00", "3" = "#56B4E9")) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Visit code", y = "Participants"
  ) 


```

There are some missing values in `n_put_in_vagina`, we replace them with 0.

```{r}

vaginal_insertions <- 
  vaginal_insertions |>
  mutate(
    n_put_in_vagina = case_when(
      as.character(n_put_in_vagina) %in% c("", NA) ~ "0",
      TRUE ~ as.character(n_put_in_vagina)
    )
  )

```

### Deleting duplicate values

As for the previous variable, some values are duplicated. We will remove these duplicates by keeping only the highest value for each participant on each study day.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 13

vaginal_insertions |> 
  filter(!is.na(n_put_in_vagina)) |>
  filter(randomized) |>
  arrange(pid, study_day) |>
  group_by(pid, study_day) |>
  mutate(n_duplicates = n()) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(
    x = study_day, y = pid, 
    col = n_duplicates |> as.character()
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(site ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    "Number of values per study_day",
    values =
      c("0" = "transparent", "1" = "#bdcedb", "2" = "green4", "3" = "orange")) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Study day", y = "Participants"
  ) 

```

The graph shows that most duplicates come from weekly samples, as expected from the study protocol. We'll first plot confusion matrices to see if these duplicates mostly agree with each other.

```{r}

duplicates <- 
  vaginal_insertions |> 
  select(pid, study_day, n_put_in_vagina) |>
  arrange(pid, study_day) |>
  group_by(pid, study_day) |>
  filter(n()==2) |>
  mutate(duplicate_nb = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = duplicate_nb, 
    values_from = n_put_in_vagina, 
    names_prefix = "n_put_in_vagina_") |>
  select(n_put_in_vagina_1, n_put_in_vagina_2) 

tab <- table(duplicates$n_put_in_vagina_1, duplicates$n_put_in_vagina_2)

tab_df <- as.data.frame(tab)
names(tab_df) <- c("n_put_in_vagina_1", "n_put_in_vagina_2", "freq")

ggplot(tab_df, aes(x = n_put_in_vagina_1, y = n_put_in_vagina_2, fill = freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = freq), color = "black", size = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#2166ac", name = "count") +
  labs(
    x = "n_put_in_vagina 1",
    y = "n_put_in_vagina 2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

We see that most duplicate values agreed with each other.

We’ll now remove duplicates using `slice_max()` (so we keep the highest `n_put_in_vagina` values).

```{r}
vaginal_insertions <- 
  vaginal_insertions |>
  select(uid, pid, study_day, visit_type, n_put_in_vagina) |>
  group_by(pid, study_day) |>
  slice_max(order_by = n_put_in_vagina, with_ties = FALSE)
```

We add the summary variables for sexual activity and semen exposure to the `calc_vars_visits` table in the metadata of the `mae` object.

```{r}
mae@metadata$calc_vars_visits <- 
  mae@metadata$calc_vars_visits |> 
  left_join(
    vaginal_insertions |> 
      select(pid, study_day, n_put_in_vagina),
    by = join_by(pid, study_day)
  )
```

## Supplementary antibiotics 

Antibiotic use was captured through two CRFs. CRF31 was completed at each clinical visit and recorded any concomitant medications reported by the participant. CRF20, part of the "Follow-up behaviour questionnaire", asked participants whether they had used any of the following in the past week: oral probiotic, vaginal probiotic, oral antibiotic, vaginal antibiotic, oral yeast medication, vaginal yeast medication, lubricant during sex, lubricant during masturbation or vibrator use, or none of the above.

### CRF 31 - Concomitant medications

CRF31 is not in the `visits_crfs_merged` or `participant_crfs_merged` datasets but in the `crf_data_clean` object.

```{r}


crf31 <- 
  metadata(mae)$crf_data_clean$crf31 |> 
  left_join(
    colData(mae) |> 
      as_tibble() |> 
      select(pid, ITT, mITT, PP, randomized, site) |> 
      distinct()
    ) |> 
  filter(randomized)

crf31 |> 
  dplyr::count(medication) |> 
  gt::gt(caption = "Concominant medication")

```

Some of those medications are antibiotics, which may have an impact on the vaginal microbiome and thus on the primary outcome. We look at the number of participants who took these antibiotics and when they took them. 


```{r}

antibiotics <- c("METRONIDAZOLE", "FLAGYL", "NITROFURANTOIN", "MACROBID", "AZITHROMYCIN", "PENICILLIN", "AMOXICILLIN", "AUGMENTIN", "CIPROBAY", "CIPROFLOXACIN", "CEFTRIAXONE", "DOXYCYCLINE","FOSFOMYCIN", "BENZANINE", "URIZONE")

# crf31 |> 
#   filter(str_detect(medication, paste(antibiotics, collapse = "|"))) |> 
#   dplyr::count(medication) |> 
#   gt::gt(caption="Supplementary antibiotics")


crf31 |> 
  filter(str_detect(medication, paste(antibiotics, collapse = "|"))) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_PP = sum(PP, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = medication
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |> 
  gt::gt(caption = "Supplementary antibiotics")

```

*Note : stars represent participants not included in the PP population*

```{r}

suppl_antibiotics_crf31 <- 
  crf31 |> 
  filter(str_detect(medication, paste(antibiotics, collapse = "|"))) |>
    mutate(
    antibiotics_cat = case_when(
      str_detect(medication, regex("METRONIDAZOLE|FLAGYL", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Metronidazole",
      str_detect(medication, regex("NITROFURANTOIN|MACROBID", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Nitrofurans",
      str_detect(medication, regex("AZITHRO", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Macrolides",
      str_detect(medication, regex("PENICILLIN|AMOXICILLIN|AUGMENTIN", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Penicillins",
      str_detect(medication, regex("CIPROFLOXACIN|CIPROBAY", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Fluoroquinolones",
      str_detect(medication, regex("CEFTRIAXONE", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Cephalosporins",
      str_detect(medication, regex("DOXYCYCLINE", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Tetracyclines",
      str_detect(medication, regex("FOSFOMYCIN", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Fosfomycin",
      str_detect(medication, regex("BENZANINE", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Benzanines",
      str_detect(medication, regex("URIZONE", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Urizone",
      TRUE ~ "Other_or_non_abx"
    ), 
    med_stop_relative_date = ifelse(is.na(med_stop_relative_date), med_start_relative_date, med_stop_relative_date), 
    pid_label = ifelse(!PP, paste("(*) ", pid), pid)
  ) |> 
    select(pid, medication, indication, med_start_relative_date, med_stop_relative_date, antibiotics_cat, PP, pid_label, site)

```

```{r}
#| fig.height: 8
#| fig.width: 8

suppl_antibiotics_crf31 |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(
    x    = med_start_relative_date,
    xend = med_stop_relative_date,
    y    = pid_label,
    color = antibiotics_cat
  ) +
    annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = -Inf, xmax = 35,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2
  ) + 
  geom_segment(linewidth = 1.2, lineend = "round") +
  geom_point(
    data = suppl_antibiotics_crf31 |> 
      filter(med_start_relative_date == med_stop_relative_date),
    aes(x = med_start_relative_date),
    size = 1
  ) +
  facet_grid(site ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Study day",
    y = "Participant",
    color = "Antibiotic",
    title = "Periods of additional antibiotic use", 
    caption = "(*) Randomized participants not included in the per-protocol population"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,100, by=7))

```

We have to re-structure the data to have one row per participant and per study day, with a variable indicating which supplementary antibiotics were taken on that day.If a participant took multiple supplementary antibiotics on the same day, we will concatenate the names of these antibiotics in the same cell, separated by a ";".


```{r}

suppl_antibiotics <- 
  suppl_antibiotics_crf31 |> 
  #filter(med_start_relative_date <= 35) |> 
  select(pid, med_start_relative_date, med_stop_relative_date, antibiotics_cat) |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(study_day = list(med_start_relative_date:med_stop_relative_date)) |> 
  unnest(study_day) |> 
  select(pid, study_day, supplementary_antibiotics = antibiotics_cat) |> 
  ungroup() 

suppl_antibiotics <- 
  suppl_antibiotics |> 
  group_by(pid, study_day) |>
  summarise(
    supplementary_antibiotics = paste(supplementary_antibiotics, collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

### CRF 20 - Antibiotics

In the CRF20 it was ask wheter the participants took antibiotics (vaginal or oral) or any probiotics (vaginal or oral) or something for yeast, lubricant, etc. during the past week. This CRF was fill every clinical visit (from V1 to V9). 

For this data, we know if a participants took antibiotics during the past week but we don't know the exact day of antibiotic use.

One participant (068200457) have a empty value ("", and not `NA`). We will consider this value as missing.

```{r}

crf20 <- 
  metadata(mae)$visits_crfs_merged |> 
  left_join(
    colData(mae) |> 
      as_tibble() |> 
      select(pid, ITT, mITT, PP, randomized, site) |> 
      distinct()
    ) |> 
  filter(randomized) |>
  select(pid, visit_code, study_day, PP, site, used_during_past_week) 

crf20 |> 
  dplyr::count(used_during_past_week) |> 
  gt::gt(caption = "Antibiotics/probiotics use during the past week, by visit")

```

We only look at the vaginal/oral antibiotics, yeast medication and probiotics use during the past week.

```{r}

suppl_antibiotics_crf20 <- 
  crf20 |>
  filter(str_detect(used_during_past_week, "antibiotic|yeast|probiotic")) |> 
  mutate(
    used_during_past_week = str_remove(used_during_past_week, "lube_with_sex, "), 
    pid_label = ifelse(!PP, paste("(*) ", pid), pid)
  )
 
suppl_antibiotics_crf20 |> 
  dplyr::count(used_during_past_week) |> 
  gt::gt(caption = "Antibiotics/probiotics use during the past week, by visit")

suppl_antibiotics_crf20 |> 
  mutate(
    used_during_past_week = used_during_past_week |> factor(
      levels = c("oral_antibiotic", "vaginal_antibiotic", "oral_yeast", "vaginal_yeast", "oral_antibiotic, oral_yeast", "oral_probiotic", "vaginal_probiotic")
    )
  ) |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = study_day, y = pid_label, color = used_during_past_week) +
  geom_point() +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = -Inf, xmax = 35,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_grid(site ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    "Medication use during the past week",
    values = c(
      "oral_antibiotic" = "deeppink", 
      "vaginal_antibiotic" = "deeppink3", 
      "oral_yeast" = "orange", 
      "vaginal_yeast" = "orange4", 
      "oral_antibiotic, oral_yeast" = "purple", 
      "oral_probiotic" = "lightblue",
      "vaginal_probiotic" = "lightblue4"
      )
  ) +
   scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Study day",
    y = "Participant",
    color = "Medication use during the past week",
    title = "Medication use during the past week (CRF20)", 
    caption = "(*) Randomized participants not included in the per-protocol population"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,100, by=7))

```

We want to see if some supplementary antibiotics were not reported in CRF31 but were reported in CRF20. We look at a window of 7 days before the study day of the visit where CRF20 was filled. The following table shows the antibiotics use reported in CRF20 and CRF31 for each participant, for each visit of CRF20. The rows are colored in pink when there is no overlap between the two CRFs, i.e. when the participant reported taking antibiotics during the past week in CRF20 but did not report any antibiotic use in CRF31 during the corresponding 7-day window, or vice versa. The rows are colored in darker pink when there is no overlap and when the visit of CRF20 occurred before day 35. This allows us to identify potential discrepancies between the two CRFs that may have an impact on the primary outcome, which is assessed at day 35.

```{r}

suppl_antibiotics_crf20 <- 
  suppl_antibiotics_crf20 |> 
  mutate(
    window_start = study_day - 7,
    window_end   = study_day
  )

suppl_antibiotics_crf20_crf31 <-
  suppl_antibiotics_crf20 |> 
  select(pid, crf20_weekly_visit = visit_code, crf20_start = window_start, crf20_end = window_end, antibiotics_crf20 = used_during_past_week, PP, pid_label) |>
  left_join(
    suppl_antibiotics_crf31 |> 
      select(pid, crf31_start = med_start_relative_date, crf31_end = med_stop_relative_date, antibiotics_crf31 = antibiotics_cat),
    by = "pid",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    overlap = !is.na(crf31_start) & crf31_start <= crf20_end & crf31_end >= crf20_start
  ) 

suppl_antibiotics_crf20_crf31 |>
  select(pid_label, crf20_weekly_visit, crf20_start, crf20_end, antibiotics_crf20, crf31_start, crf31_end, antibiotics_crf31, PP, overlap) |>
  arrange(overlap, is.na(crf31_start), PP) |>  
  gt() |>
  tab_style(
    style = 
      cell_fill(
        color = "coral1", alpha = 0.1),
        locations = cells_body(rows = !overlap)
  ) |> 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "coral1", alpha = 0.3),
    locations = cells_body(rows = crf20_start <= 35)
  ) |> 
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "coral1", alpha = 0.7),
      locations = cells_body(rows = !overlap & PP & crf20_start <= 35)
    )

```


We merged the add the information of CRF20 in the `suppl_antibiotics` dataset, incorporing new rows for the visits where antibiotics were reported in CRF20 but not in CRF31. We also created a variable `antibiotics_source` to indicate whether the information on supplementary antibiotics came from CRF20, CRF31, or both.

```{r}

suppl_antibiotics_crf20 <- 
  suppl_antibiotics_crf20 |>
  # Separate multiple entries ("oral_antibiotic, oral_yeast")
  separate_rows(used_during_past_week, sep = ",\\s*") |>
  mutate(
    is_antibiotic = str_detect(used_during_past_week, "antibiotic")
  ) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(study_day = list(window_start:window_end)) |>
  unnest(study_day) |>
  select(pid, study_day, used_during_past_week, is_antibiotic) |>
  ungroup()

suppl_antibiotics_crf20_to_add <-
  suppl_antibiotics_crf20 |>
  left_join(
    suppl_antibiotics |> select(pid, study_day, crf31_med = supplementary_antibiotics),
    by = c("pid", "study_day")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    already_in_crf31 = !is.na(crf31_med) & is_antibiotic,
    # Keep if: non-antibiotic (always) OR antibiotic not in CRF31
    keep = !already_in_crf31
  ) |>
  filter(keep) |>
  select(pid, study_day, supplementary_antibiotics = used_during_past_week)

# combined dataset of supplementary antibiotics from both CRF31 and CRF20
suppl_antibiotics <- 
  suppl_antibiotics |>
  mutate(source = "CRF31") |>
  bind_rows(
    suppl_antibiotics_crf20_to_add |> mutate(source = "CRF20")
  ) |>
  group_by(pid, study_day) |>
  summarise(
    supplementary_antibiotics = paste(supplementary_antibiotics, collapse = "; "),
    source = paste(unique(source), collapse = " & "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

```{r}

tmp <- 
  suppl_antibiotics |>
  separate_rows(supplementary_antibiotics, sep = ";\\s*") |>
  arrange(pid, supplementary_antibiotics, study_day) |>
  group_by(pid, supplementary_antibiotics, source) |>
  mutate(
    gap = study_day - lag(study_day, default = dplyr::first(study_day) - 1) > 1,
    segment_id = cumsum(gap)
  ) |>
  group_by(pid, supplementary_antibiotics, source, segment_id) |>
  summarise(
    start = min(study_day),
    end   = max(study_day),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    visits_crfs_merged |> select(pid, site, PP) |> distinct(),
    by = "pid"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    pid_label = ifelse(!PP, paste("(*) ", pid), pid)
  )

# Graphe
tmp |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(
    x     = start,
    xend  = end,
    y     = pid_label,
    color = supplementary_antibiotics,
    linetype = source
  ) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = -Inf, xmax = 35,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_segment(linewidth = 1.2, lineend = "round") +
  geom_point(
    data = tmp |> filter(start == end),
    aes(x = start),
    size = 1
  ) +
  facet_grid(site ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "CRF31"          = "solid",
      "CRF20"          = "dotted",
      "CRF31 & CRF20"  = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x        = "Study day",
    y        = "Participant",
    color    = "Medication",
    linetype = "Source",
    title    = "Periods of supplementary medication use",
    caption  = "(*) Randomized participants not included in the per-protocol population"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 7))

```

We add the summary variables for sexual activity and semen exposure to the `calc_vars_visits` table in the metadata of the `mae` object.

```{r}
mae@metadata$calc_vars_visits <- 
  mae@metadata$calc_vars_visits |> 
  left_join(
    suppl_antibiotics |> 
      select(pid, study_day, supplementary_antibiotics, source_supplementary_antibiotics = source),
    by = join_by(pid, study_day)
  )
```
